content:
Apple is about to unveil its two flagship new iPhones: the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. The Pro series has a clear price advantage, but the following points will make the iPhone 18 Pro outperform the more expensive Ultra model in many ways.

#1: Main camera with variable aperture

There are rumors that the iPhone 18 Pro's main camera will receive a major upgrade, including the addition of a variable aperture feature. The iPhone Ultra is not expected to include this feature.

Rumors about the variable aperture have been circulating for some time, but we still don't know exactly how Apple will implement it. This feature is expected to significantly improve Portrait mode, offer new levels of depth-of-field control, and deliver notable improvements in low-light photography.

The components required for the variable aperture are expected to be larger than those in the current main camera, so the ultra-thin iPhone Ultra is unlikely to adopt this feature.

#2: Pro Max offers longer battery life

According to regulatory filings, while the iPhone Ultra should have decent battery life, the Pro series—especially the iPhone 18 Pro Max—will still deliver the longest battery life of any iPhone to date.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max is reportedly getting a physical battery that's 10% larger than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and combined with efficiency gains from the A20 Pro and C2 chips, battery life is bound to be the best ever on an iPhone.

Because the iPhone Ultra features a unique foldable design, it's hard to judge its battery life based on specs alone, but the ultra-thin design paired with a smaller physical battery inevitably means it won't be able to keep up with the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

#3: Face ID

For the first time in years, a flagship iPhone model won't include Face ID. The iPhone Ultra will only feature Touch ID.

Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro will continue using the Face ID system that has been around for nearly a decade.

Apple reportedly couldn't free up enough space in the ultra-thin iPhone Ultra design for the Face ID components. Full support would require double the components: one set for the outer display and another for the inner display. So when it comes to authentication, the iPhone 18 Pro will have a clear edge.

#4: Telephoto lens

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will continue to be the only models with a telephoto lens. The iPhone Ultra will only have a main camera and an ultrawide lens, with no telephoto lens for optical zoom.

For many users who rely on a telephoto lens, this could be a major differentiator between the two. Especially since there are rumors that Apple will further upgrade the telephoto lens this year with a larger aperture.

If you want the best camera system, the iPhone 18 Pro is the obvious choice.

Bonus: The traditional iPhone experience

Strictly speaking, this isn't a feature, but it's worth mentioning. For many users, the iPhone 18 Pro offering a "traditional" iPhone experience is already a significant advantage.

The iPhone Ultra will be very different from any model that came before it. The size and shape of the inner and outer displays will feel somewhat unfamiliar to iPhone users, and using it requires folding and unfolding rather than operating a single screen—something that may take time to get used to.

The current iPhone form factor has always been hugely popular with users. While foldable devices certainly have their fans, I expect that for the average consumer—especially those who have never visited 9to5Mac—the traditional design of the iPhone 18 Pro will be the reason many people choose it.

Which new iPhone model are you planning to buy this fall? Let us know in the comments.
